newsitem.title: USA: Midwestern governors ask ethanol subsidy be kept.
newsitem.headline: Midwestern governors ask ethanol subsidy be kept.

text.p: Governors of 12 midwestern states have sent letters to U.S. House Speaker Newt Gingrich and minority leader Dick Gephardt urging them to retain ethanol subsidies in tax legislation currently moving through Congress, Iowa Governor Terry Branstad said Monday.
"There should be no messing with ethanol. Tax credit for ethanol should be maintained as is," Branstad told reporters after a meeting of Republican governors in Washington.
Legislation which cleared the House Ways and Means Committee last week included removal of the subsidy, but Branstad said he was confident that that would be changed before passage of the bill.
Branstad said Republican governors, who control most states in the midwest, had written to Gingrich, while the Democrats had addressed their appeal to Gephardt.
Republicans control North Dakota, South Dakota, Minnesota, Iowa, Kansas, Ohio, Michigan, Illinois and Wisconsin.
Democrats control Nebraska, Indiana and Missouri.
